claims.text: The dynamic behavior of as-solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn is governed by an interplay between dislocation mobility and strain-induced deformation twinning or minor TRIP.
Mn-induced local chemical disorder modulates the strain-induced microstructural evolution of FeNiCrMn.
At lower temperatures and higher strain rates, local lattice distortions inhibit dislocation glide in FeNiCrMn.
Impeded dislocation glide at lower temperatures and higher strain rates promotes deformation twinning or minor TRIP.
Deformation twinning contributes to increased strain hardening.
Twinning or minor TRIP maintains the strength-ductility balance of dynamically loaded FeNiCrMn.
At elevated temperatures, thermal activation increases dislocation mobility in FeNiCrMn.
Increased dislocation mobility at elevated temperatures suppresses deformation twinning.
Suppression of twinning at elevated temperatures produces a smoother flow-stress response.
As-solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn has a fine, largely homogeneous microstructure.
The initial FeNiCrMn microstructure contains inherent Mn-induced chemical disorder.
Increasing strain rate will increase the yield strength of FeNiCrMn, especially at lower temperatures.
FeNiCrMn will exhibit heightened strain hardening at lower temperatures and higher strain rates.
Lower-temperature, high-rate deformation will produce more deformation twins or minor phase changes in highly strained regions.
Elevated-temperature deformation will show reduced twin formation and more pronounced thermal softening.
Related Co-containing and Al-containing high-entropy alloys exhibit substantial strain-rate sensitivity.
Dislocation activity and mechanical twinning have been reported as dynamic deformation and hardening mechanisms in related high-entropy alloys.
Quasi-static mechanical-performance data support the strength-ductility balance of Co-free FeNiCrMn.

contradictions.description: The initial state and test conditions specify as-solidified samples, whereas the boundary describes the material as both as-solidified and homogenized. A homogenization treatment is ordinarily a post-solidification processing step, so the tested state is ambiguous.
